title: GitHub - lusob/model-booster: A lab where Opus brews smart pills for a tiny JS neural net by writing its weights directly (weight-space programming)
excerpt: A lab where Opus brews smart pills for a tiny JS neural net by writing its weights directly (weight-space programming) - lusob/model-booster
content_html:
A visual lab for weight-space programming (Takehi et al., MIT CSAIL, 2026: an LLM writes a network's weights directly, without gradient descent).

Bit is a tiny untrained network (MLP 600→256→64→5, tanh, about 170k weights) that runs in your browser. With all-zero weights it just wanders. A smart pill is a set of weights that Opus writes in code, through claude -p. Give Bit a pill and watch it play properly. Drag the dose slider to blend the weights from zero to the pill and watch the behaviour change.

Try it online: https://lusob.github.io/model-booster/. The online lab is a showcase: Bit and every pill on the shelf run in your browser, but brewing new pills needs Opus and a small server on your own computer: see Install it locally.

Install it locally

Install the lab on your computer to brew your own pills. Brewing runs locally because the lab server drives the Claude Code CLI, which writes the weights. You need Node.js 20+ and a logged-in claude CLI that can use Opus.

git clone https://github.com/lusob/model-booster.git
cd model-booster
npm install
npm run dev

Then open http://localhost:5173. npm run dev starts the lab server on :8787 and Vite on :5173. Pick a starter recipe or write your own in the brewing station and press Brew pill with Opus. "Opus's notebook" shows each design and test live, and the finished pill lands on the shelf. A brew usually takes a few minutes and spends Claude usage (capped by BREW_MAX_USD, default 15).

If headless calls fail with "OAuth session expired", run claude once in a terminal and /login.

To share your pills, commit the new files in public/pills/ and push. The GitHub Pages workflow republishes the online lab.

How a pill is brewed (server/brew.ts)

  1. Objective. A starter recipe has its scoring built in. For a custom recipe, Opus first turns your text into event points and a game config (server/brief.ts, objectivePrompt).
  2. Workspace (brews/<id>/). It holds BRIEF.md (rules, observation layout, model spec, and the paper's method), build.mjs (Opus writes the circuit here), lib.mjs (helpers with no forward pass), try.mjs (the forward-pass budget: 20 tries of 64 practice episodes each), and game-source.ts.
  3. Opus. claude -p --model claude-opus-5-5 runs with only Read/Write/Edit plus node build.mjs and node try.mjs allowed. Its progress streams to the UI over SSE.
  4. Grading. The lab grades weights.json on 128 held-out levels against silly Bit and saves the result to public/pills/<id>.json.

You can also brew from the terminal: npm run brew -- catch-all dodge or npm run brew -- --game catch "Catch only blue balls". If a brew is interrupted, npm run bottle -- brews/<brew-id> <starter-id> grades and bottles the last weights it built.

Environment knobs: BREW_MODEL, BREW_TRIES (default 20), BREW_TIMEOUT_MIN (40), BREW_MAX_USD (15), LAB_PORT (8787).

Note: build.mjs is code that Opus writes and that runs on your machine through node. The budget is enforced by try.mjs, and Opus is trusted not to run its own evaluator.

Games (src/core/games/)

All games share one 10×10×6 observation (agent, wall, red, green, blue, trail), so one body can take any pill. The games are Catch, Dodge, Bounce, Collector, Maze, Flutter (flap through gaps), Ring (boxing), Snake, Swarm (space shooter), and Crossing (cross the road). Each one emits events (caught:red, died, reached:goal…) that recipes turn into scores.

Wiring test

npm run ref checks a few hand-written circuits (scripts/circuits.ts) against silly Bit. It's a test that the games and the model are wired correctly. Those circuits are never put on the shelf, so every pill there was brewed by Opus.

Deploying

.github/workflows/pages.yml builds the static site (npm run build, output dist/) and publishes it to GitHub Pages on every push to main. In the repo settings, Pages must use GitHub Actions as its source.
